offsiteOpportunities.name: Show HN launch post
offsiteOpportunities.relevance: Show HN readers are exactly the self-hosted and personal-software audience that wants a dice-driven reading queue, and a launch post is an earned mention rather than a purchased link.
offsiteOpportunities.notes: One genuine launch announcement, written for the audience. Do not repost it later to re-drive traffic, and do not ask for a second front page.

offsiteOpportunities.name: awesome-selfhosted list
offsiteOpportunities.relevance: ComicPile is a self-hosted application with no external service dependencies, which is exactly what this curated list catalogs for people who run their own infrastructure.
offsiteOpportunities.notes: The list has an explicit contribution process: a working project, a description, and a license. The entry is earned by meeting the list criteria, never by trading links.

offsiteOpportunities.name: Comics reader communities
offsiteOpportunities.relevance: Comic collectors repeatedly ask what to read next from a growing stack; a dice-driven queue answers that question with the reader's own history instead of a generic recommendation list.
offsiteOpportunities.notes: Only post where the community rules allow it, contribute to the discussion first, and make the post useful to readers who will never use ComicPile. Expect moderation to remove a thin promotion.

offsiteOpportunities.name: Indie product directories
offsiteOpportunities.relevance: Directories for personal software projects already host tools with a comparable audience and let the maintainer describe the problem the tool solves, which suits a small self-hosted project without a marketing team.
offsiteOpportunities.notes: List the product once, write an honest description, and keep the listing maintained. Do not submit the same listing to many directories in bulk; that is link spam.

offsiteOpportunities.name: Product launch platforms
offsiteOpportunities.relevance: A launch platform gives a personal project one concentrated day of discovery from people who actively look for new tools, which is more efficient than scattered link building.
offsiteOpportunities.notes: Submit only a working product, and treat it as a launch date rather than a link farm. A maker badge or an upvote is not a durable citation, so do not depend on it.
